extraction_text: King Vasu (also known as Go) ruled the kingdom of Chedi as a righteous king who sometimes enjoyed hunting.

attributes.details: King Vasu, a descendant of the Puru dynasty, ruled Chedi following Indra's guidance.

extraction_text: King Vasu abandoned his weapons and lived in a forest hermitage to practice asceticism.

attributes.details: He engaged in severe penance in the forest.

extraction_text: Indra, fearing King Vasu might become the king of gods through his asceticism, appeared before him with a thunderbolt to dissuade him.

attributes.details: Indra used persuasion to stop King Vasu's ascetic practices.

extraction_text: Indra advised King Vasu to uphold dharma (righteousness) on earth, promising him eternal divine worlds and friendship.

attributes.details: Indra emphasized protecting dharma and offered friendship, with Indra in heaven and Vasu on earth.

extraction_text: Indra described Chedi as a prosperous, fertile, and righteous land, urging King Vasu to live there.

attributes.details: Chedi was praised for its wealth, climate, and adherence to dharma by all castes.

extraction_text: Indra gifted King Vasu a divine flying chariot made of crystal, a victory garland (Indra's garland), and a bamboo staff.

attributes.details: The chariot allowed flight, the garland offered protection in battle, and the staff was for protecting the learned.

extraction_text: King Vasu, in reverence to Indra, planted the bamboo staff in the earth at the year's end.

attributes.details: He honored Indra by planting the staff as a symbolic act.

extraction_text: From ancient times until today, virtuous earth protectors have erected poles like King Vasu did.
The next day, kings erected tall poles decorated with flower baskets, sandalwood, garlands, flowers, and ribbons.
Lord Shankara (Indra) accepted this joyful form of worship in the human world and became fond of noble King Vasu.

attributes.relationship: Indra develops fondness for King Vasu

extraction_text: Great Indra saw King Vasu's excellent offerings and was pleased, declaring that those who worship him and establish his festival like King Vasu will prosper, win victories, and have wealthy, happy people.

attributes.relationship: Indra blesses King Vasu and his followers

extraction_text: Indra, filled with joy, bestowed deep favor upon King Vasu.
King Vasu had five heroic, radiant sons and made them kings in different countries.
The five sons were: Prithu (chariot warrior, famous king of Magadha), Pratishthala, Kaushambi (also called Ratnavaha), Machira, and Yadu (victorious hero).
King Vasu entered Indra's heavenly palace, traveled in a crystal flying chariot, and was welcomed by Gandharvas and celestial maidens, earning him the name 'High Conduct' (Uparichara).

attributes.action: Ascension to heaven and celestial travel

extraction_text: The Shankhini River flowed toward King Vasu's capital but was intercepted by the amorous Kolahala Mountain.
King Vasu kicked Kolahala Mountain, creating a gap through which the Shankhini River flowed.
Kolahala Mountain and Shankhini River had twin children. The river, now free, happily gave the children to King Vasu.

attributes.relationship: Mountain and river as parents, King as adoptive father

extraction_text: King Vasu made the boy the army commander (a hero who subdues enemies) and married the girl, named Girika (Mountain-born).

attributes.relationship: King adopts son as commander, marries daughter

extraction_text: One day, King Vasu's wife Girika told him her menstrual period had arrived, and she bathed to be pure for conceiving a son.
On that same day, the ancestors told King Vasu to go hunt deer.
King Vasu (婆薮王) went hunting in the forest while thinking of his wife, the mountain maiden (山娘).
King Vasu's semen (元阳) accidentally flowed out while walking in the forest, and he caught it with a leaf.
King Vasu recited a spell to prevent the semen from spoiling and asked a swift eagle to deliver it to his wife, the mountain maiden, as it was her fertile period.
Another eagle, mistaking the semen for meat, attacked the first eagle, causing the semen to fall into the Yamuna River (阎牟那河).

attributes.action: Aerial Fight and Loss of Semen

extraction_text: The celestial maiden Adrika (石姑), cursed by Brahma (大梵天) to live as a fish, swallowed the semen in the Yamuna River.

attributes.supernatural_element: Curse and transformation into a fish

extraction_text: Fishermen caught the pregnant fish after ten months and found a boy and a girl inside her.

attributes.action: Catching Fish and Discovery of Children

extraction_text: King Uparichara Vasu (高行王) took the boy, named him Matsya (摩差, meaning 'fish'), who later became a righteous king.
Adrika was freed from her curse upon giving birth to human children and returned to her celestial form, ascending to the heavens.

attributes.supernatural_element: Curse fulfillment and transformation back to celestial form

extraction_text: The girl, named Satyavati (贞信), was given to a fisherman by the king and grew up with a fish-like scent.
The maiden (later revealed as Satyavati) was rowing a boat on the water to be filial to her father when the sage Parashara saw her during his pilgrimage.
Sage Parashara, captivated by Satyavati's beauty, immediately proposed to make love to her.
Satyavati expressed concern about being seen by other sages on the riverbanks, so Sage Parashara created a dense fog to conceal them.
Satyavati further objected, citing her virginity and duty to her father, worrying about her reputation.
Sage Parashara promised Satyavati she would remain a virgin after their union and offered her a boon.
Satyavati chose the boon of having a delightful body fragrance, which Sage Parashara granted.
Satyavati and Sage Parashara united, after which she became known as 'Gandhavati' (Fragrant One) and 'Yojanagandha' (Fragrance Traveling a Yojana).
Sage Parashara departed, and Satyavati gave birth to their son on an island in the Yamuna River.
The newborn son (Vyasa) immediately turned to asceticism and told his mother he would appear whenever she thought of him for needed tasks.
Vyasa, observing the decline of righteousness and human capabilities across ages, divided the Vedas into four parts to preserve them, earning the name 'Vyasa' (Compiler).
Vyasa taught the four Vedas and the Mahabharata to his disciples including his son Shuka, and through them the epic was disseminated.
Bhishma, the son of King Shantanu and the river goddess Ganga, is born with great valor and fame.

attributes.relationships: Bhishma is the son of King Shantanu and Ganga.

extraction_text: An old sage, known as 'Shankha Muni' (Spear-tip Muni), is falsely suspected of theft and impaled on a spear.
Shankha Muni calls upon Dharma (the god of righteousness) and confesses to killing a bird with a reed in his childhood.

attributes.relationships: Shankha Muni appeals to Dharma for judgment.

extraction_text: Dharma curses Shankha Muni to be reborn from a Shudra woman's womb for the sin of killing a Brahmin, which is considered more severe.

attributes.action: Dharma curses Shankha Muni to be reborn as Vidura.

extraction_text: Dharma is reborn as Vidura from a Shudra woman, becoming learned, righteous, and flawless.

attributes.relationships: Vidura is the rebirth of Dharma.

extraction_text: Sanjaya, the charioteer, is born from Gavalgama, equal to a sage.

attributes.relationships: Sanjaya is the son of Gavalgama.

extraction_text: Karna, the warrior, is born from the sun god Surya and the virgin Kunti, with innate armor and earrings.

attributes.relationships: Karna is the son of Surya and Kunti.

extraction_text: Vishnu, the supreme god, is manifested by Vasudeva and Devaki to bless the worlds.

attributes.relationships: Vishnu is manifested through Vasudeva and Devaki.

extraction_text: Vishnu is described with various divine attributes and names, such as the creator, the imperishable soul, and the highest being.
Vishnu is born into the Andaka-Vrishni clan for the development of righteousness.

attributes.relationships: Vishnu incarnates in the Andaka-Vrishni clan.

extraction_text: Two great warriors, Satyaki and Kritavarma, skilled in weapons and devoted to Narayana (Vishnu), are born from the Satvata and Hridika clans.

attributes.relationships: Satyaki and Kritavarma are devoted to Vishnu.

extraction_text: Drona is born from the semen of Bharadvaja, which falls into a wooden vessel through the power of a sage's severe austerities.

attributes.relationships: Drona is the son of Bharadvaja.

extraction_text: Ashwatthama's mother and the mighty Kripa are born from the semen of Gautama's son Shardwan, which falls into a reed bed.

attributes.relationships: Ashwatthama's mother and Kripa are children of Shardwan.

extraction_text: Drona later fathers Ashwatthama, a foremost warrior.

attributes.relationships: Ashwatthama is the son of Drona.

extraction_text: Dhrishtadyumna is born from the sacrificial fire, resembling the fire god Agni, to destroy Drona.

attributes.relationships: Dhrishtadyumna is born to kill Drona.

extraction_text: Draupadi is born from the sacrificial altar, radiant and extremely beautiful.
After the birth of Naganjaya, the disciple of Prahlada, Shakuni is born as a punishment of righteousness due to the anger of the gods.

attributes.relationships: Shakuni is born as a divine punishment.

extraction_text: King Shakuni of Gandhara fathers Shakuni (son) and Gandhari (daughter, mother of Duryodhana), both knowledgeable in 'artha' (prosperity).

attributes.relationships: Shakuni and Gandhari are children of King Shakuni of Gandhara.

extraction_text: The sage Krishna Dvaipayana (Vyasa) begets King Dhritarashtra and the mighty Pandu in the field of King Vichitravirya.

attributes.relationships: Dhritarashtra and Pandu are sons of Vyasa, born posthumously for King Vichitravirya.

extraction_text: King Janamejaya asks the Brahmin about the kings not yet mentioned and why the god-like warriors were born on Earth.

relationships: King Janamejaya asks Brahmin for information

extraction_text: The Brahmin (Shaunaka) states he will reveal the secret of the gods after worshipping Brahma.

relationships: Shaunaka prepares to answer King Janamejaya

extraction_text: Parashurama (Jamadagni's son) exterminated the Kshatriyas from Earth twenty-one times and then performed penance on Mount Mahendra.
After Parashurama created a world without Kshatriyas, Kshatriya women sought conception from Brahmins.

relationships: Kshatriya women approach Brahmins for offspring

extraction_text: Brahmins, strictly disciplined, lay with Kshatriya women during their menstrual periods without lustful impulse.
Thousands of Kshatriya women conceived from Brahmins and gave birth to many brave Kshatriya boys and girls.

relationships: Brahmins as fathers, Kshatriya women as mothers

extraction_text: The Kshatriyas were reborn through Brahmins with ascetic power and Kshatriya women, flourishing with righteousness and long life, re-establishing the four castes with Brahmins as the highest.
All beings, including humans and other creatures, began mating only during menstruation, not driven by lust but not missing the menstrual period.
All beings flourished by adhering to dharma, enjoyed long lifespans, and were free from afflictions and diseases.

attributes.relationships: Universal adherence to dharma

extraction_text: The earth, bounded by oceans, was intact with mountains, plains, forests, and protected by Kshatriyas.

attributes.relationships: Kshatriyas as protectors of the earth

extraction_text: Kshatriyas ruled the earth with dharma, bringing supreme happiness to all varnas, with Brahmins as foremost.

attributes.relationships: Kshatriyas ruling justly, Brahmins as leaders

extraction_text: Kings abandoned faults born of desire and anger, punished sinners with dharma, and protected the people.

attributes.relationships: Kings as protectors of people

extraction_text: Indra (also known as Sakra or Hundred-Sacrifices) sent sweet rain at proper times and places due to Kshatriyas upholding dharma, ensuring prosperity.

attributes.relationships: Indra supporting Kshatriyas' adherence to dharma

extraction_text: No children died young, and no men engaged with women before becoming youths.

attributes.relationships: Moral conduct

extraction_text: The earth was filled with long-lived people.
Kshatriyas performed many grand sacrifices with generous gifts, and Brahmins studied the four Vedas, including Vedangas and Upanishads.

attributes.relationships: Kshatriyas supporting Brahmins' studies

extraction_text: Brahmins did not sell scriptures for money or recite Vedas near Shudras.

attributes.relationships: Brahmins maintaining purity

extraction_text: Vaishyas plowed land with bulls, did not yoke cows, and cared for weak cattle; milk was not taken while calves suckled.

attributes.relationships: Humane treatment of cattle

extraction_text: Merchants did not sell deceptive goods, and people acted only as dharma prescribed, keeping it in mind and heart.

attributes.relationships: Universal adherence to dharma

extraction_text: All varnas performed their duties, and dharma was strong everywhere.

attributes.relationships: Each varna fulfilling its role

extraction_text: Cows and women gave birth on time, trees bloomed and bore fruit in all seasons.
The earth was filled with various beings in the perfectly functioning Krita Yuga (Golden Age).
Asuras, defeated by Adityas in battle and expelled from heaven, were born on earth among kings and various beings to seek divine status.

attributes.relationships: Asuras vs. Adityas, Asuras seeking power

extraction_text: Asuras took birth in cows, horses, kings, donkeys, camels, bulls, carnivorous beasts, elephants, and deer, overwhelming the earth.

attributes.relationships: Asuras infiltrating earthly beings

extraction_text: Daityas (sons of Diti) and Danavas (sons of Danu) fell from their world to the human realm.
Daityas and Danavas became powerful, arrogant, and occupied the Earth, tormenting all classes (Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras) and other creatures.
Earth Goddess (Prithvi) could not bear the weight and torment, so she sought refuge with Brahma.
Brahma, already aware of the situation, promised Earth Goddess to unite the gods to address it.
Brahma commanded all gods to incarnate on Earth using parts of their bodies to relieve Earth Goddess's burden.
Brahma also commanded Gandharvas and Apsaras to incarnate on Earth as they wished.
Gods, led by Indra, accepted Brahma's command and approached Narayana (Vishnu) for their incarnations.

Vishnu is described with divine attributes including holding a discus and mace, wearing yellow clothes, emanating dark radiance, having a lotus from his navel, and possessing large, beautiful, curved eyes.
Indra requests Vishnu to incarnate partially for the purification of the earth.
Vishnu agrees to Indra's request.
